title: A local model button on the first-run sign-in screen

steps.path: The screen a brand-new install shows after it finishes installing, before the app opens
steps.headline: How should the local model option appear on the sign-in screen?
steps.today: The sign-in card has a filled Log in with Claude button, outlined Log in with ChatGPT and Log in with OpenRouter buttons, and a small underlined link reading "Use an API key or local model".
steps.problem: That link only opens a box for an Anthropic API key. Someone who wants to run a model on their own computer has no way through setup at all.
steps.proposal: Give local models their own way in. Pick how prominent it should be.

options.label: A fourth button
options.summary: An outlined "Use a local model" button under the three sign-in buttons, the same size as them.
pros: Reads as an equal choice, not a hidden extra.
Log in with Claude stays the one filled button, so the screen still has one main action.
cons: The card grows by one more button's height.

options.label: Its own small link
options.summary: A second underlined link beside the API key one, reading "Use a local model".
pros: The card stays the size it is today.
cons: Easy to miss, and makes running on your own computer look like an afterthought.

options.label: A separate section
options.summary: A thin divider under the sign-in buttons with "Or run it on this computer" and a button below it.
pros: Makes clear this is a different kind of choice: no account, nothing leaves your computer.
cons: The tallest of the three; on a small laptop screen the card may need scrolling.

steps.path: After pressing the new local model option
steps.headline: After pressing it, where does setting up the local model happen?
steps.today: Local models are set up in Settings, on the Local Models page: install the model runner first, then pick a model and download it.
steps.problem: A new user has never seen Settings. Sending them there means they arrive in an app with nothing to chat with until they find that page and finish two downloads.
steps.proposal: Choose whether setup walks them through it or hands them to the page that already exists.

options.label: Inside setup
options.summary: The sign-in card turns into a short local model setup: install the runner, choose a model, download it, then the app opens.
pros: They leave setup with an assistant that can answer straight away.
Same flow as signing in: finish on this screen, then the app opens.
cons: A new screen to design, on top of the Local Models page that already does this.

options.label: Open the Local Models page
options.summary: Setup finishes immediately and the app opens straight onto Settings, Local Models.
pros: Uses the page that already exists, so it ships sooner.
They learn where local models live for later.
cons: That page is built for people who already know what an engine and a quant are.
Nothing stops them closing it and landing in a chat that cannot answer.

steps.path: The local model setup, at the step where a model is chosen
steps.headline: How should a new user choose which model to download?
steps.today: The app ships 11 recommended models in three groups by computer memory: small (about 8 GB), everyday (16 to 32 GB) and large (32 GB or more). It can already tell whether a model fits this computer.
steps.problem: A new user has no way to judge which of 11 names is right for their computer, and a model that does not fit either will not load or runs very slowly.
steps.proposal: Choose how much of that choice setup makes for them.

options.label: One suggestion
options.summary: Setup suggests the best model that fits this computer, with a "Choose a different model" link that opens the full list.
pros: One button to press; the right answer for most people.
Anyone who knows what they want can still pick.
cons: The suggestion is the app's judgement, and a slow computer gets a less capable model.

options.label: The full list
options.summary: All 11 models, each marked Fits, Tight or Too large for this computer.
pros: Nothing is hidden or chosen for them.
cons: 11 unfamiliar model names at the moment they know least about them.

options.label: Always the smallest
options.summary: Setup always downloads the same small model; bigger ones can be added later in Settings.
pros: Fastest download, and it runs on nearly any computer.
cons: A powerful computer gets a weaker assistant than it could run, and first impressions suffer.

steps.path: The local model setup, while the model downloads
steps.headline: While the model downloads, should the app wait or open?
steps.today: Downloading a model on the Local Models page shows a progress bar there. A model is usually a few gigabytes, so the download can take many minutes.
steps.problem: Waiting on a setup screen for ten minutes feels broken, but opening an app that cannot answer yet is confusing too.
steps.proposal: Choose what they see during the download.

options.label: Wait on setup
options.summary: The setup card shows the download's progress and time left, with a Back button to choose a sign-in instead; the app opens when it finishes.
pros: When the app opens, it works.
Back is always there if the download is too slow.
cons: Nothing to do but watch a progress bar for the length of the download.

options.label: Open while downloading
options.summary: The app opens right away; the message box says the model is still downloading and shows its progress until it is ready.
pros: They can look around the app while they wait.
cons: Their first experience is a message box they cannot use yet.
More places in the app have to handle "not ready yet".

steps.page: What setup installs, and what happens when things go wrong
steps.intro: The first page decided how the option looks and flows. These decide what setup does around it.

steps.path: The install checklist a new install runs before the sign-in screen
steps.headline: Should setup still install Claude Code for someone who only wants a local model?
steps.today: Every new install downloads Node, Git and Claude Code before the sign-in screen appears, whichever sign-in the person then picks.
steps.problem: Someone choosing a local model does not use Claude Code, so they wait for a download they may never need.
steps.proposal: Choose whether that install is kept or skipped for them.

options.label: Keep installing it
options.summary: Setup stays in the order it runs today; the local model option simply appears on the sign-in screen.
pros: Signing in to Claude later needs nothing more to install.
Setup's order is untouched, so nothing else can break.
cons: A local-only user waits for an install they do not use.

options.label: Ask first, then install
options.summary: The sign-in choice moves to the start of setup, and Claude Code is only installed for people who pick Claude.
pros: Local-only users get through setup sooner.
cons: Reorders every new user's setup, including the Claude path that works today.
Signing in to Claude later would first have to install it.

steps.risk: Moving the question to the start changes the first minutes of every new install, not just local ones.

steps.path: The local model option, on a computer with little memory
steps.headline: What should happen on a computer too small to run a model well?
steps.today: The app can tell how much memory a computer has and whether each model fits, but nothing on the sign-in screen uses that.
steps.problem: On an 8 GB laptop even the smallest model is slow, and someone who picks local there may think the whole app is slow.
steps.proposal: Choose whether and how setup warns them.

options.label: Show it, with a warning
options.summary: The option is always there; on a small computer setup says the model will be slow and suggests signing in instead.
pros: Nobody is locked out of the choice.
They pick knowing what to expect.
cons: One more sentence on an already busy screen, for those computers.

options.label: Hide it
options.summary: Computers below a memory limit do not see the option at all.
pros: Nobody has a bad first experience from it.
cons: Someone who wants privacy over speed cannot choose it.

options.label: No warning
options.summary: Every computer sees the same option, with no mention of speed.
pros: Simplest screen.
cons: The slow experience arrives with no explanation.

steps.path: Reopening the app after quitting partway through local model setup
steps.headline: If someone quits before the model finishes downloading, where should the app reopen?
steps.today: The app reopens on the sign-in screen when nothing usable is set up. But once the model runner alone is installed, it counts as set up, even with no model downloaded.
steps.problem: Quitting mid-download would reopen straight into an app that cannot answer, with no hint why.
steps.proposal: Choose where they land when they come back.

options.label: Back to setup
options.summary: Until a model is downloaded, the app reopens on the setup screen, which offers to resume the download.
pros: They pick up exactly where they left off.
Closes the gap where an app with no model counts as set up.
cons: Someone who meant to set up the model later in Settings is sent back to setup until they do.

options.label: Open the app
options.summary: The app opens normally, with a notice that no model is downloaded yet and a button to finish.
pros: Never blocks them from the app.
cons: They can still start a conversation that cannot answer.

steps.path: The small underlined link under the sign-in buttons
steps.headline: What should happen to the "Use an API key or local model" link?
steps.today: The link opens a box for an Anthropic API key, which is passed to Claude Code.
steps.problem: Once local models have their own option, the words "or local model" point at something the link does not do.

options.label: "Use an Anthropic API key"
pros: Says exactly what it does.
cons: Names a company some users will not recognise.

options.label: "Use an API key"
pros: Shorter, and matches the wording it has today.
cons: Someone with an OpenAI or OpenRouter key may try theirs and see it fail.

steps.path: The phone app's own setup screens
steps.headline: This change is desktop only: the phone app has no local models and its own separate setup screens.
steps.changed: Stated, not asked: the Android app cannot run local models at all today, and it never shows this sign-in screen.
steps.notice: Phones keep their current setup exactly as it is. Local models on Android would be a separate project.
